dataset.title: A Dynamic Plasticity Model for Rapidly-Heated 1045 Steel up to 1000 °C
dataset.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
dataset.method: Compression using a Kolsky bar and a servohydraulic test machine
dataset.coverage_note: Counts are CSV experiment blocks. Some experiments appear in more than one table. The high-temperature tests are concentrated at high strain rates after rapid heating.

related_evidence.condition: Rolled and normalized bar before hot compression
related_evidence.data_access: Published fit coefficients and plots. The article says raw data are available from the authors on request.
related_evidence.use: Compare lower-rate hot flow under the study heating protocol. Keep this condition distinct from the NIST rapid-heating dataset.
Cross-check observed phase changes under the experimental welding thermal histories.

related_evidence.condition: AISI 1045 plate with heat treatment unspecified
related_evidence.data_access: Table 1 reports conductivity and volumetric heat capacity with replicate standard deviations. Equations 7 and 8 fit those data.
related_evidence.use: Check low-temperature thermal magnitudes. Volumetric heat capacity has units J/(m³ K) and requires a separate density to infer mass-specific heat.

related_evidence.condition: Ferrite–pearlite C45 variants with different thermomechanical histories
related_evidence.data_access: Chapter 3, Figures 50, 54, 58 and 66. Density, heat capacity, diffusivity and compression plots.
related_evidence.use: Compare microstructure sensitivity. The lower-rate compression program uses 20, 500 and 680 °C at 0.5, 5 and 50 s⁻¹. The author reports that machine compliance limits Young modulus inference. These data do not reach the hot-forging range.

hot_compression_reference.condition: Conventionally rolled and normalized bar, heated at 5 °C/s under vacuum

calibration_gaps: Reconcile initial condition and deformation-rate coverage for the selected forging grade.
Validate the published hot flow fit before adapting it to granular mechanics. Finite-strain compression flow stress does not establish zero-strain yield strength.
Source thermal properties, ductility and heat-treatment behavior for the selected condition before catalog activation.

held_out_compression_reference.inputs: Initial specimen temperature and measured true stress at shared strain values. Temperature-dependent fit uses the nearest retained run on each side. No published fitted stress column is used.
held_out_compression_reference.scope: One full intermediate-temperature run withheld at a time, with end runs retained to avoid extrapolation. Initial temperatures span 711–1007 °C and nominal rates span 4078–4718 s⁻¹ across the nine source runs. Rate and thermal history are coupled in this experimental series. The result does not establish a general rate-dependent constitutive law, an initial yield value or forging calibration.
